note: Re-judged 2026-11-02 by an independent auditor who authored none of the changes named. RFC 7911 Section 3: "However, the Path Identifier MUST be assigned in such a way that the BGP speaker is able to use the (Prefix, Path Identifier) to uniquely identify a path advertised to a neighbor." Producers moved in 5f0aa168c2 (one recovery-owner answer per source per write: release now clears the cached answers) and 217c3e6fd5 (entries from a per-table slot store: clearRoutes clears the store, recordDeletion frees the slot after its last read, and the per-NLRI closures of recordSection and filterSection became the pooled walk's methods recordNLRI and allowNLRI in session_ownership_walk.go, now cited in the code map). Re-read: recordNLRI keeps the identifier logic byte-for-byte (takeReleased hands a released receipt's identifier reservation to the new entry, otherwise fwdPathIDs.retain(key.path.received) for an ADD-PATH key), a reused slot is zeroed so it carries no other key's owner, and recordDeletion still calls keepReleased or releasePath before the slot is freed. None mints an identifier, passes a received one through, or lets two paths share one toward a neighbor. Both tagged units are byte-identical and still require a stable identifier across updates and different identifiers for colliding sources. Verdict unchanged: enforced.
